inputs.text: This “grassroots” campaign looks less like an open debate and more like a managed push to shape the rules before the public can examine them. Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is promoting a petition to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration…”—then the wording stops before the proposal is complete. That omission is the tell: people are being rallied around a slogan while the full terms remain hidden. I’d be wary of who benefits from keeping the details out of sight.

output.main_topic: Criticism of Water Not Coal’s petition and its incomplete proposal wording
subtopics: Concerns about public scrutiny and hidden terms
output.narrative_frame: Skeptical framing of the campaign as a potentially managed effort that rallies people around a slogan while the proposal’s full terms remain undisclosed.
opinions: The campaign looks more like a managed push to shape rules than an open debate.
The omission of the proposal’s full wording is presented as a warning sign.
The writer recommends being wary of who benefits from the details remaining hidden.
